cards.text: Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, is writing to believers he calls foreigners and exiles. He's just told servants to submit to their masters, and he pointed to Christ, who suffered without fighting back. Now he turns to wives: in the same way, submit yourselves to your husbands.

cards.question: Peter says some husbands refuse to believe the word. How can those husbands be won over?

answers.text: Without words by how their wives live
By hearing their wives preach to them
By a visit from the church elders

cards.text: Peter says those husbands will see their wives' pure and reverent demeanor, no speech needed. It's like a fresh batch of cookies, friend: nobody has to announce them, because the smell walks into the room FIRST.
Then Peter says beauty shouldn't come from outward adornment, like braided hair, gold jewelry or fine clothes. I'm standing on a GOLD base over here, friend, and I FELT that one.

cards.question: If beauty shouldn't come from braided hair, gold or fine clothes, where does Peter say it should come from?

answers.text: The inner disposition of the heart
A lifetime of hard and honest work
The respect of the whole town

cards.question: Peter calls a gentle and quiet spirit precious in God's sight, but says its beauty fades with time.
Peter says this is how the holy women of the past adorned themselves. They put their hope in ___ and were submissive to their husbands.

cards.text: Then Peter names one of those women: Sarah, Abraham's wife. He says she obeyed Abraham and called him lord.

cards.question: Peter tells the wives they're Sarah's children if they do what is right. And what must they refuse to do?

cards.text: Then Peter turns to the husbands, with that line again: in the same way. He tells them to treat their wives with consideration, as a delicate vessel.

cards.question: Peter also tells husbands to honor their wives. What does he call those wives?

answers.text: Fellow heirs of the gift of life
Guests to be served with care

cards.question: Peter says the way a husband treats his wife has nothing to do with his prayers.
Finally Peter speaks to all of them. He tells them to be like-minded, but to keep their feelings for each other to themselves.
Peter tells all of them to love as brothers and be tenderhearted and humble. Then: do not repay evil with evil or insult with insult, but with ___.

cards.text: Peter says they were called to this, so that they may inherit a blessing. So that fiery reply you typed in the group chat at midnight, friend, gets a big old DELETE.

cards.question: Peter backs this up with a quote about whoever would love life and see good days. That person must keep his ___ from evil, turn from evil and do good, and seek ___ and pursue it.

cards.text: Not wait for peace. PURSUE it, friend, the way I once chased one runaway chocolate chip across my whole bakery, hopping on this gold base the ENTIRE way.

cards.question: Peter's quote ends with the eyes and ears of the Lord. Whose prayer does it say His ears are inclined to?

cards.text: Then the quote's last line: "But the face of the Lord is against those who do evil." Wives, husbands, all of you: Peter just made sure nobody got left out of this batch.

findings.problem: The opening card states facts from outside the passage but gives them no reference. It says Peter is an apostle of Jesus Christ (1 Peter 1:1) and that he calls his readers foreigners and exiles (1 Peter 2:11). It also says he just told servants to submit to their masters and pointed to Christ, who suffered without fighting back (1 Peter 2:18-23). The card cites only 1 Peter 3:1.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: The right answer, 'The inner disposition of the heart', uses the passage's formal Bible wording. The two wrong answers are plain modern phrases ('A lifetime of hard and honest work', 'The respect of the whole town'), so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: This story card only repeats 'seek peace and pursue it', which card 16 already covered, and adds a joke. It tells no new part of the passage, so it is a recap card.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage.

findings.problem: The question says Peter's quote 'ends with the eyes and ears of the Lord.' That isn't true. The quote ends with 'But the face of the Lord is against those who do evil' (1 Peter 3:12), and card 19 even calls that line 'the quote's last line.'

rule.text: What he points out must be true.
